4: Facilitator script (opening): The performance review conversation is the moment where evidence is examined, progress is acknowledged, gaps are named, and course corrections are agreed. It is where performance management actually happens.
This unit makes that conversation a genuine conversation about execution reality: grounded in evidence, focused on progress, and committed to recovery when things go off track.
5: The pattern in many organisations: In many organisations, enormous effort goes into designing strategy. Leaders invest months clarifying direction, defining OKRs, setting targets, and aligning teams around ambitious outcomes. Scorecards are built. KPIs are cascaded. Performance frameworks are communicated.

Yet several months later, when leadership teams pause and reflect, the same uncertainty often appears. Work is happening. Teams are busy. Initiatives are underway. Leaders still cannot confidently answer a more fundamental question: “Is the work being done actually advancing the strategy?” This is the gap that performance measurement exists to close.

The visibility infrastructure: Performance measurement creates the visibility infrastructure that allows leaders to observe whether the organisation is genuinely progressing toward its strategic outcomes. Without this infrastructure, strategy remains largely interpretive. Each function develops its own sense of progress. Activity becomes mistaken for advancement. Energy is expended, but the connection to the enterprise result becomes difficult to see.
Performance measurement restores that line of sight. It allows the organisation to move from activity visibility to progress visibility.
What activity measures give: Counts of projects launched, meetings held, campaigns executed and deliverables completed create a sense of operational movement.
6: Course correction (further detail): Without early signals, problems are discovered only when targets have already been missed.
With and without measurement: Without measurement, strategy remains largely aspirational. With measurement, strategy becomes manageable.

Execution rhythm: Performance measurement creates execution rhythm. Most strategic outcomes are the result of cumulative progress built over time. Teams experiment, adjust, learn, and refine their approach as they move forward. Because of this, progress must be observed repeatedly across weeks, months, and quarters.

Regular review cycles allow leaders to notice the subtle signals that indicate whether execution is strengthening or weakening. Momentum may begin to accelerate in one area while slowing in another. Resource constraints may appear. Decision bottlenecks may surface. Capability gaps may become visible. When these signals are visible early, leaders can respond while the situation is still manageable.

This rhythm prevents the most common leadership surprise in organisations: discovering performance failure only at the end of the reporting period. Performance measurement ensures that strategy is observed while it is unfolding, as well as evaluated after the fact.

A leadership practice: Within the Strategy2Results® system, performance measurement is understood as a leadership practice as well as a reporting mechanism. It shapes how leaders observe execution reality, how they engage their teams in evidence-based dialogue, and how they guide the organisation through obstacles and adjustments.

Review signals priority: The act of regularly reviewing evidence communicates something powerful throughout the organisation. It signals priority. Teams pay attention to what leaders review. When performance evidence is consistently examined, discussed, and acted upon, people understand that execution outcomes matter. Attention naturally flows toward the priorities that receive leadership scrutiny.

If a KPI appears on a scorecard but never appears in leadership conversations, the organisation quietly concludes that the KPI does not truly matter. When performance evidence becomes part of the regular leadership dialogue, accountability strengthens and focus sharpens.

From data to execution intelligence: At this point, performance measurement begins to evolve beyond data collection. It becomes execution intelligence. Data on its own rarely improves performance. Numbers simply describe what has happened. Insight emerges only when those numbers are interpreted through disciplined conversation. Performance measurement therefore transforms data into decision insight.
Each review cycle helps leaders answer three essential questions:
1. What progress has been achieved since the last review?
2. What obstacles are preventing further progress?
3. What adjustment will restore momentum toward the target?

Through these conversations, performance management becomes a learning system. Teams develop a deeper understanding of how strategy unfolds in practice. Leaders strengthen their ability to guide execution through uncertainty and complexity.

Scorecards and review discipline: Many organisations successfully build scorecards. Far fewer build the review discipline required to make those scorecards meaningful. The difference between the two determines whether performance management becomes a compliance ritual or a genuine engine of execution progress.
Through disciplined review conversations, organisations transform performance data into insight, insight into action, and action into renewed progress toward their strategic results.
7: From visibility to conversation: Once performance measurement makes execution visible, the next challenge is to translate performance visibility into meaningful conversations that restore momentum. The cycle transforms raw data into insight, and insight into action, so that performance measurement does not end with a score being recorded.

The stagnation the cycle prevents: Many organisations collect performance data but fail to convert that data into disciplined action. Reports are produced, dashboards are circulated, and metrics are displayed, yet very little actually changes in the way work is executed. The Review–Realign–Restore Cycle prevents this stagnation by creating a structured rhythm through which performance evidence is examined, interpreted, and acted upon. Through this cycle, performance measurement becomes a living execution discipline.

Review (further detail): The self-assessment requires more than assigning a score: it requires the submission of verifiable evidence. Process indicators also count as evidence. The leader responsible for overseeing the KPI reviews the same KPI and examines the submitted evidence.

The existence of these two perspectives is intentional. Self-assessment encourages ownership and reflection by the KPI owner. Leader assessment introduces strategic perspective and broader organisational context. By examining both assessments together, the review conversation becomes a joint sense-making exercise.
The three review questions shift the conversation away from opinion and toward observable progress. The review stage therefore creates the visibility necessary for meaningful leadership action.
Realign (further detail): The three root causes and their recovery responses are set out in full in the notes of the Accountability Loop slide.
Restore (further detail): Execution momentum is restored through disciplined follow-through. The updated alignment score provides an ongoing signal of organisational readiness for execution.

Why the cycle matters: The Review–Realign–Restore Cycle transforms performance measurement into an execution recovery system. Without this cycle, measurement becomes historical reporting. Numbers describe what happened in the past but provide little guidance about what should happen next.

With this cycle in place, measurement becomes a dynamic leadership process. Leaders observe progress. They diagnose emerging obstacles. They intervene intelligently. They restore momentum before performance failure becomes systemic.

Over time, this discipline builds an organisation that measures performance and continuously restores it. That capability is one of the defining characteristics of organisations that consistently convert strategy into results.
8: Why gaps arise: Market conditions shift. Internal dependencies create delays. Capabilities evolve more slowly than anticipated. Competing priorities emerge. The realignment stage assigns no blame.

The default response: Many organisations respond to performance gaps with one default response: they push harder. More urgency is applied. More pressure is introduced. Deadlines are reinforced. Pressure alone rarely solves execution challenges because pressure does not identify the underlying cause of the problem. The Accountability Loop focuses on diagnosing the root cause of the gap.

Lack of accountability (in full): The work may feel detached from a meaningful outcome. Competing priorities may have diluted attention. Personal energy may have shifted elsewhere. When this condition appears, the leader revisits the broader organisational context of the KPI. The conversation reconnects the task to the enterprise outcome it supports. The individual is reminded how their contribution fits into the wider organisational map. By restoring that line of sight, motivation and commitment can often be reactivated.

Lack of skill (in full): The challenge may involve technical expertise, analytical capability, leadership skills, or process knowledge that was initially underestimated. When the root cause is skill-related, the response focuses on capability development and adds no pressure. Targeted coaching may be introduced. Peer support may be arranged. Formal training may be provided. In some cases the timeline attached to the KPI may also require adjustment if the capability development process requires additional time.

Misfit of role or structural constraint (in full): Sometimes the issue lies beyond motivation and skill development. The role may require capabilities that the individual does not naturally bring to the task. In these cases the conversation shifts toward structural alignment. The task may be redistributed across the team. Responsibilities may be adjusted. In some situations the individual may be repositioned into a role that better aligns with their strengths.

The leadership principle behind the separation: Performance discussions focus on progress toward outcomes. Role alignment discussions focus on placing individuals where their capabilities can generate the greatest organisational value. By maintaining this distinction, the organisation protects both fairness and clarity.
10: Strategy design is rarely the differentiator: Leadership teams articulate compelling visions, define ambitious OKRs, and cascade KPIs across the organisation. The elegance of the strategy design rarely separates the organisations that sustain execution momentum from those that quietly stall.

The rhythm of conversations: Organisations that consistently convert strategy into results rely on more than the strength of the original plan. They rely on a rhythm of disciplined performance conversations that keeps execution visible, corrects drift early, and sustains organisational focus over time.

The discipline that sustains momentum: When the review discipline operates consistently, something powerful begins to emerge inside the organisation. Execution becomes visible, discussable, and recoverable.

Leaders are no longer surprised by performance outcomes at the end of the year. They observe the trajectory of progress in real time. Teams understand that their work contributes directly to enterprise outcomes. Obstacles are surfaced while they are still manageable. Accountability remains active.

Over time, this discipline builds a culture where strategy, once announced, is continuously examined, adjusted, and advanced through structured leadership dialogue. That is what transforms performance measurement from a reporting system into a genuine execution discipline.
11: 01 · Early Warning Signals Are Missed: A further subtle indicator is a dependency between functions that introduces unexpected delays. The organisation continues operating under the assumption that progress is on track until the gap becomes large enough that recovery is far more difficult. Disciplined review conversations prevent this outcome by ensuring that progress is observed while it is unfolding.

02 · Gradual Diffusion of Accountability: When progress is regularly reviewed and discussed, KPI owners understand that their work remains connected to the organisation’s strategic priorities. Over time, without review, accountability becomes ambiguous. People assume progress is occurring somewhere in the system, yet no one feels the immediate responsibility to ensure that it actually is. Structured performance reviews prevent this diffusion by maintaining a clear line of ownership between the KPI and the individual responsible for advancing it.

03 · Loss of Organisational Learning: Execution delivers outcomes and also develops the organisation’s capability to execute increasingly complex strategies over time. When review reflections occur consistently, the organisation begins to accumulate execution intelligence. Teams develop a deeper understanding of how work actually moves through the organisation.
04 · Erodes Leadership Credibility: Every review conversation reinforces the seriousness with which the organisation treats its strategic objectives.
12: Significant Gap (further detail): This signal indicates that the organisation must diagnose the deeper conditions affecting execution.
13: Section opening: Performance measurement rarely breaks down for lack of agreed goals, targets or KPIs. The problem is rarely the absence of measurement.
As a leadership conversation discipline, performance measurement determines whether the executive team can see execution reality clearly and intervene early enough to maintain momentum.
14: Gap 01 · Horizontal Coordination: In the functional reviews, Technology evaluates system delivery. Customer experience depends on marketing promises, operational delivery, technology reliability, and service responsiveness. Revenue growth depends on sales capability, product readiness, pricing discipline, and operational fulfilment.

The cross-functional sessions sit alongside the functional reviews and serve a different purpose. The conversation shifts from “How is my function performing?” to “How is the execution system performing?” When leaders observe performance through this collective perspective, interdependencies become visible and coordination improves.

Gap 02 · Evidence Quality: When the evidence standard becomes consistent across functions, performance conversations regain their diagnostic power. Leaders spend less time debating data and more time improving execution.

Gap 03 · Review Rhythm Breakdown: Measurement is a continuous execution responsibility for KPI/KR owners. The Alignment Brigade protects the rhythm by ensuring that review conversations occur with the consistency required to detect early signals of drift.
Gap 04 · Learning Suppression: Over time the organisation becomes more effective at measuring performance and at improving how performance is produced.
16: The risk the collective guards against: Performance reviews fragmenting into isolated departmental conversations, where leaders see only isolated functional success.
17: Round 1 (further detail): The percentage each leader states involves no estimate and no narrative opinion. The purpose of this round is to establish a shared baseline understanding of enterprise execution momentum.
Round 2 (further detail): Once a warning is recognised as a cross-functional execution dependency, the Alignment Brigade can intervene before the issue evolves into a measurable performance gap.
Round 3 (further detail): The learning may involve a capability insight, a coordination improvement, a leadership practice that strengthened execution, or a structural obstacle that slowed progress.
What the circle produces: When the Collective Intelligence Circle is completed, the executive team achieves three outcomes.
First, the organisation gains a clear snapshot of enterprise progress toward its strategic Key Results.
Second, emerging risks become visible early enough for coordinated intervention.
Third, the organisation captures execution learning that strengthens future performance.

This conversation transforms performance measurement from a departmental reporting exercise into an enterprise intelligence practice. The executive team begins to see how the strategy is moving across the organisation in real time.
Through this practice, performance measurement becomes the organisation’s radar system for strategy execution.
18: Position on the board: The synthesis layer is a fourth section added across the bottom of the board, titled “Enterprise Intelligence Synthesis”.
20: Zone 1: % progress toward Key Results / KPIs; supporting evidence (from PM review sheets); momentum signal (accelerating, stable or slowing).
Zone 2: one or two early warning signals; evidence from PM reviews; potential impact area (optional but recommended).
Zone 3: one key execution insight; evidence from PM reviews; where it applies (function or enterprise).
Board flow (how the board is used in the session):

Round 1, Populate Trajectory: each CXO posts their entry into Zone 1: “We are at X% progress, supported by [evidence], and momentum is [state].” Outcome: a visible enterprise execution baseline; immediate visibility of uneven progress.

Round 2, Populate Warning Signals: each CXO posts into Zone 2: “An emerging risk is [signal], supported by [evidence].” Outcome: early-stage risks become visible; cross-functional dependencies begin to surface.

Round 3, Populate Execution Learning: each CXO posts into Zone 3: “A key execution learning is [insight], supported by [evidence].” Outcome: practical intelligence on how execution actually works; patterns of effectiveness and friction emerge.

What this board achieves: When built and used correctly, the board delivers a real-time view of enterprise execution; early visibility of systemic risks; a growing base of execution intelligence; and a shift from departmental reporting to collective decision-making.
21: Purpose of the exercise: This exercise simulates a situation where performance has fallen significantly below target and the leader must activate the Accountability Loop using the Review–Realign–Restore framework.

Brief to the CXO: You are the CXO responsible for ensuring progress toward the Key Result. Your objective is to diagnose the root cause of the performance gap without immediately blaming the individual. Conduct the conversation using the Accountability Loop, then use the alignment dialogue to restore momentum.
23: The unit in one view: The Performance Measurement unit establishes the review discipline that keeps strategy execution visible and correctable. It recognises a fundamental execution reality: strategy fails when progress is not consistently examined, however strong the leaders’ intention.

Performance measurement therefore creates the visibility infrastructure that allows the organisation to observe whether work across functions is actually advancing the Success in Practice. The unit progresses through four stages that strengthen this execution visibility.
Extrapolating (Where): Leaders examine where performance measurement commonly weakens across the executive system.

Integration (Collective): The executive team synthesises their performance insights through a Collective Intelligence Circle built on evidence from their PM review sheets. Each CXO contributes three signals: progress confirmation, early warning indicators, and execution learnings.
